cornerCallouts: Into Copse now, a deceptively fast right-hander that requires absolute commitment. The cars are glued to the tarmac as they navigate this crucial corner.
Brooklands is next, a challenging left-hander that tests the drivers' braking skills. It's easy to lock up here and run wide.
Luffield, a long, sweeping right-hander, demands precision and control. The drivers need to carry as much speed as possible through this corner.
Woodcote, the final corner on the National layout, is crucial for a good run down the start/finish straight. A clean exit is essential.
The Wellington Straight, a high-speed blast that allows the drivers to stretch their legs. Top speeds will be reached here.
After the Wellington Straight, the cars brake hard for Brooklands, a good overtaking opportunity.
The run from Copse to Brooklands is short but vital, as drivers jockey for position and prepare for the braking zone.
The exit of Luffield is critical for setting up a good run onto the final straight, so getting the power down is paramount.
strategyPoints: With the shorter National layout, tire degradation might be less of a factor than on the full Grand Prix circuit, but managing them is still crucial.
Fuel consumption will be less of a concern on this shorter layout, allowing teams to potentially run a more aggressive engine mode.
The pit window here is relatively short, so teams need to be precise with their timing to avoid losing valuable track position.
A well-timed safety car could significantly impact the race outcome on this National layout, bunching up the field and creating opportunities.
Overtaking opportunities are limited on this circuit, making a good start and strategic pit stops even more important.
The shorter lap length means drivers will be encountering traffic more frequently, requiring them to be patient and opportunistic.
With fewer high-speed corners, the setup will likely favor mechanical grip over aerodynamic downforce on this National layout.
The lighter fuel load on the shorter layout could lead to some daring overtakes late in the race as drivers push to the limit.
